newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST-Siam Cement Q1 seen down 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Siam Cement Q1 seen down 23 pct.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said on Wednesday it expected Siam Cement Plc to post a consolidated net profit of two billion baht ($76.9 million), or earnings per share of 16.7 baht, in the first quarter of this year.
That would be down 23 percent from the 2.6 billion baht profit it posted in the same quarter of 1996.

Merrill Lynch said in a report that the drop in earnings at one of Thailand's largest industrial conglomerates would be mainly due to a weaker contribution from ceramic tiles, petrochemicals and auto accessories.
Siam Cement is scheduled to announce its first-quarter results later today.
"The divisions which should post stronger earnings growth in Q1 1997 are the cement and steel divisions," the report said.

It added that the company, Thailand's largest cement producer, would see higher first-quarter earnings growth in its cement business, driven by capaciy expansion of 4.2 million tonnes per year in the fourth quarter of last year.
Siam Cement's annual cement production is at 21 million tonnes, it said.
Merrill Lynch still recommended investors to accumulate Siam Cement shares due to the low price earnings ratio of 8.9 times of its 1997 estimate earnings.
Siam Cement had dipped 18 baht to 518 on volume of 8,600 shares by 0425 GMT.
